scores.critique: Strongest edge/fleet engineering of the three (distance-triggered sampling, thermal callbacks, store-and-forward, signed OTA, 1 Hz trip_fix telemetry that makes clean-pass verification and bus-exposure actually computable) and the cleanest state machine/DB schema. But as a hackathon deliverable it is the least credible to finish: the 7-day plan simultaneously commits to a Kotlin Android app, a Jetson/Hailo runner, an OSRM build, PMTiles for all Telangana, RF-DETR verifier training and a full PWA, and it ignores the Python 3.11 venv with verified CUDA that already exists on the box (plans a fresh 3.12 venv + torch cu130). Depth: method is sound (metric mono -> RANSAC plane -> camera-height scale lock -> depth-below-plane integral -> Z^2-weighted Kalman), but there is no uncertainty attached to each measurement, no synthetic known-cavity unit test, and the demo credibility rests on 'self-shot Hyderabad clips to be collected on day 2' and RDD frames with a guessed fx/h, so the jury sees numbers it cannot check. depth_max = 98th percentile is reasonable, but no treatment of crowned/rutted roads (global plane only, 25 mm RMSE reject will throw away many real Indian roads). IMU is only a trigger, not a corroborating depth source. From the GHMC engineer's seat: work-order batching and MB export are there, but no audit log, no escalation chain, no daily indent, no jurisdiction-unknown queue. YOLO26/FastAPI 0.162/PG18 version claims are unverified for all three designs.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: 1 Hz trip_fix telemetry with cam_active flag (the only honest basis for 'clean pass' auto-closure and bus-exposure counts); jolt-only observations for water-filled/night potholes; split DBSCAN clusters by lateral offset >1.5 m for adjacent lanes; signed (ed25519) model OTA with ETag config; metered-upload rules keyed to GPS accuracy and queue age; separate storage of cavity volume vs square-cut design volume to show the saving vs cuboid; greedy 500 m same-owner work-order batching.

scores.critique: The only design that treats the user's hard requirement (depth -> volume -> bags) as the first thing to build and to prove: measurement record carries value + sigma + method tag (mono/mono+imu/stereo/lidar/manual), explicit error propagation (sigma_Z = k*Z^2, plane RMS, sigma_A, sigma_V), a local quadratic road surface for crowned/rutted roads instead of a single global plane, IMU quarter-car corroboration gated on wheel-path lane offset, a synthetic hemispherical-cavity exact-volume unit test, and a staged foam-board known-depth target filmed with a checkerboard-calibrated phone: this is a demo a jury can verify on the spot, with no special hardware. It also uses the existing Python 3.11 venv (torch cu128 on RTX 5080 verified) instead of fighting 3.14, and the build order delivers a single-image end-to-end 'measure run' + bag count by step 6 so a partial deliverable exists early. What it gets wrong: DBSCAN with min_samples=2 marks single-pass detections as noise, so 'candidate' potholes never get an entity unless the status machine is special-cased; the IMU '~15 % error' claim is lifted from literature and will not hold for a 12-tonne bus without a per-vehicle gain fit; 'exact bags of cold mix' in the pitch oversells a ±20-40 % single-frame volume; the age term uses days/14 which under-weights the GHMC 24 h charter; and the ops layer (no audit log, no escalation chain, no daily indent per circle, weaker jurisdiction handling) is thinner than Design 3, which matters to the engineer who must use it daily. Scope is still enormous (Android, Jetson, OSRM, planetiler PMTiles) for a hackathon.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: Measurement row with method tag + sigma, and billing gated on a minimum method quality; local quadratic road-surface fit on the 0.3-1.0 m ring; per-pixel uncertainty propagation and quality score (range, plane RMS, blur, illumination); staged foam-board target of known depth (20/40/70 mm) as the jury credibility artefact; per-bus calibration certificate (uncertified devices usable for prioritisation, not for MB billing); IMU jolt gated on wheel-path lane offset; merging potholes within 0.5 m into one square cut; patch survival curves per contractor/material/method/monsoon; using the existing 3.11 venv.

scores.critique: Best answer to 'will a GHMC executive engineer use this daily': audit_log on every state transition with actor/before/after/geo, AE -> DEE -> EE -> Zonal Commissioner escalation on SLA breach, daily per-circle 'repair run' indent (bags, CRM, emulsion, crew-hours), jurisdiction queue for unknown road owners (the exact failure of the Cyberabad CCTV pilot), contract table with DLP months and payment that can only reference verified_closed, MoRTH SDB item codes, Telugu field SOP, contractor portal. The demo path is also the most pragmatic: PostGIS nearest-way with heading filter instead of an OSRM build, a synthetic 'digital bowl' rendered into a planar image to unit-test the integration maths. Where it is weaker: depth. d_design = max(d_avg, 50 mm) is a real engineering error, a 60 mm-deep hole with 35 mm mean depth gets a 50 mm patch and the deepest part is under-filled (Designs 1/2 correctly use p95); there is no staged real-world known-depth target, so credibility rests on the synthetic bowl plus RDD frames with a guessed car calibration; CI from weighted MAD is fine but there is no per-pixel error model or quality gate; RDD box-to-mask via an eYantra-trained seg model (to stay licence-clean) will produce worse masks than SAM2. The 20-hour build order is fantasy for this scope; it splits API (3.14) and ML (3.12) venvs and ignores the existing working 3.11 venv. Exposure formula with multiplicative bonuses then 'normalised to 1' is under-specified.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: Audit log on every transition; escalation chain and SLA timers; daily repair-run indent per circle with route ordering; jurisdiction queue for unknown owners; contract/DLP table with payment gated on verified_closed and dlp_event as an evidence package rather than an automatic penalty; PostGIS nearest-way + heading fallback so the demo does not depend on an OSRM build; synthetic bowl rendered into a planar image as a maths unit test; projecting the mask centroid onto the road plane to place the pothole (not the camera) on the map; Telugu-first field SOP and admin-unit layer with validity dates for the 150/300-ward change.

winner: DESIGN 2: GunthaMeter — it is the only design that makes the user's mandatory depth/volume requirement provable on the dev machine (uncertainty-tagged measurements, local surface fit, IMU corroboration, synthetic exact-volume test, staged known-depth foam-board target) and front-loads that into a minimum viable jury demo while using the already-working Python 3.11/CUDA venv. Build it, but graft on Design 3's operations layer (audit log, escalation chain, daily circle indent, jurisdiction queue, payment gated on verified_closed, PostGIS nearest-way fallback) and Design 1's 1 Hz trip telemetry with cam_active for honest clean-pass verification; fix DBSCAN min_samples so single-pass candidates get an entity, keep d_design on p95 not mean, and drop 'exact bags' language in favour of bags ± sigma.

scores.critique: Widest scope of the three and therefore the most likely to arrive half-built: 9 phases covering a Kotlin Android app, Jetson runner, OSRM build, PMTiles, WhatsApp bot, MB export and a 100-pothole field campaign in 7 days. Depth validation leans on '10-20 self-shot Hyderabad clips with tape-measured potholes' — there is no bench test (synthetic cavity or staged target) that can be run on the dev box today, so the jury sees numbers nobody can check. Pins Python 3.12 and ignores the Python 3.11 venv already present on the machine. DBSCAN with min_samples=1 means every single false positive becomes a 'candidate' entity in my queue. Its own worked example contradicts its formula (claims 0.7x0.6 cut from 0.5x0.4 with 0.10-0.15 m margin each side, which is 0.70-0.80 x 0.60-0.70; fine, but the 2m notation elsewhere says +0.25 total). No audit log, no AE->DEE->EE escalation ladder, no per-circle daily indent, so as an EE I still have to turn the priority list into an indent by hand. The jolt-only observation and 'water-filled -> depth unknown' handling are honest, but Table 5.3 stretch rating and contractor DLP breach are asserted rather than engineered with evidence packages. Strongest on bus-deployment realism (DC-DC, thermal callbacks, depot Wi-Fi drain, 2,800 buses x 270 km/day) and on multi-tenant routing, but as a daily tool it is a mapping product with a work-order bolt-on.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: Distance-triggered inference (>=4 m, >=5 km/h) to kill signal-stop duplicates; 1 Hz trip_fix telemetry with cam_active so 'clean passes' are provable; jolt observations when IMU fires but camera does not; greedy 500 m work-order batching per road owner so one jet-patcher trip handles 5-20 holes; ed25519-signed OTA model config; storing both square-cut V_mix and integrated V_cavity to show the saving vs cuboid; Tier A' Pi 5 + Hailo as the heat-tolerant production path; lateral-offset split of clusters for adjacent lanes.

scores.critique: The only design that treats a measurement as value + sigma + method tag and gates Measurement-Book billing on a per-device calibration certificate — that is exactly what an EE needs when a contractor disputes a bag count. The staged foam-board pothole (20/40/70 mm) filmed with a checkerboard-calibrated phone is a demo I can watch and believe, and it correctly uses the existing Python 3.11 venv and RTX 5080 (verified: /home/coral/Desktop/Telangana pathole detection/.venv/bin/python3.11 exists, GPU is RTX 5080). The local quadratic surface fit for crowned/rutted roads and the quarter-car IMU corroboration are real engineering, not slides. Where it fails the daily-use test: no audit log, no escalation ladder, no daily per-circle indent, work orders are per pothole/cluster with no run batching, and T-age uses days_open/14 which is far too lenient against GHMC's 24-h arterial charter (the +0.3 breach bonus only partly rescues it). DBSCAN min_samples=2 contradicts the 'candidate after 1 pass' state (noise points never become entities unless special-cased). Cites a BBMP jet-patcher rate (Bengaluru) and 'IRC:SP:100 cl. 2645' (that is a MoRTH Specification clause, not SP:100) — an R&B engineer will notice. Jurisdiction and ward handling is described but thinner than Design 3; contractor liability is 'configurable' and not backed by an evidence package. Also the longest single pipeline in GPU terms (RF-DETR verifier + DA3 + SAM2 labelling) with the DB arriving only at step 8, so the ops half is at risk if measurement work overruns.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: measurements table with method{mono,mono_imu,stereo,lidar_phone,manual_gauge,citizen} + sigma columns; calibration certificate per device with 'uncertified = prioritisation only, not MB'; staged known-depth target as the jury credibility artefact; local quadratic surface instead of a global plane for crowned Indian roads; IMU quarter-car depth corroboration with per-vehicle gain; pothole ground point = GPS + IPM range/bearing (not camera position); explicit sigma propagation formulas; 'never report a water surface as pothole floor'; survival curves per contractor/material/method.

scores.critique: This is the one that reads like it was written by someone who has sat in a GHMC circle office: audit_log on every transition with actor and field lat/lon, AE->DEE->EE->Zonal Commissioner escalation on SLA timers, a daily 'repair run' indent per circle with total bags/CRM/emulsion/crew-hours, a jurisdiction queue for the GHMC/R&B/NHAI/SCB confusion, DLP events as evidence packages rather than automatic penalties (which is what will survive a contractor's lawyer), contract table with package/DLP months, rate table per FY with MoRTH SDB item codes, and pluggable admin_unit for the 150-vs-300 ward mess. PostGIS nearest-way-with-heading as the shipped demo fallback instead of a mandatory OSRM build is the right call for hackathon week. Weaknesses: d_design = max(d_avg, 50 mm) under-orders material versus cutting to sound depth (d_p95 as in Designs 1-2 is more defensible to an R&B auditor); the error model and CIs are hand-waved (weighted MAD, base 8 mm at 5 m) with no sigma-propagation and no certificate/billing gate, so depth credibility is below Design 2; verification radius 15 m vs 6 m cluster eps will count passes on the adjacent lane as 'clean'. The 20-hour build order is fantasy and the API-on-3.14/ML-on-3.12 split ignores the working 3.11 venv already on the box. Uses the seg model to pseudo-mask RDD boxes instead of SAM2, which will give worse masks for a licence benefit nobody at a hackathon cares about. No IMU depth corroboration, only a jolt scalar.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: audit_log(entity, before, after, actor, geom) on every state transition; escalation ladder AE->DEE->EE->Zonal Commissioner driven by SLA timers; daily per-circle 'repair run' indent with route ordering; jurisdiction queue for unknown road owner; contract table (package, DLP months, sla_rules) spatially joined to road_segment; DLP reopen as an evidence package (before/after/re-detection) with debit-note draft; PostGIS nearest-way + heading fallback for map matching; synthetic 'digital bowl' unit test for the volume integral; 3 clean passes AND 10% random engineer QC before auto-close; invoices only against verified_closed WOs; public per-ward transparency page.

winner: DESIGN 3: GaddaFix — from a GHMC executive engineer's seat it is the only one that produces what I actually sign every day (a per-circle indent, an auditable work-order state machine with escalation, contract/DLP linkage with evidence packages, and a jurisdiction queue), while remaining demo-able on the dev box without an OSRM build or an Android app. It should borrow Design 2's measurement schema (method + sigma + calibration certificate gating the Measurement Book, staged known-depth target, d_p95 design depth) and Design 1's trip_fix telemetry and 500 m work-order batching to close its depth-credibility gap.

scores.critique: Strongest fleet/ops systems thinking (edge-first bandwidth budget, distance sampling, IMU jolt observations, fleet redundancy as the recall mechanism, 1 Hz trip_fix telemetry for clean-pass verification, multi-tenant from day one) but it is the least measurement-rigorous of the three and the hardest to actually land in hackathon time. ML-science problems: (a) no uncertainty model at all beyond 'sigma^2 proportional to Z^2' hand-waving; nothing propagates plane RMSE or the grazing-angle sin(theta) factor into depth error, so the stored numbers have no error bars for an engineer to trust; (b) distance gating 3-15 m is too generous for a 960x540 WebP uploaded frame from a 2.4 m bus mount: at 15 m a pixel covers ~5-8 cm of road and the monocular network smooths sub-pixel cavities, so 25 mm IRC bins are below the noise floor there; (c) the full frame is downscaled to 960x540 on edge before upload, throwing away the resolution the depth stage needs; (d) global RANSAC plane only (ring region helps but no local quadratic for crowned/rutted Indian roads); (e) depth_max as 98th percentile and depth_class from p75 across tracks are ad hoc and not justified; (f) 'DA3METRIC fx*out/300' convention is asserted and validated 'once'. Feasibility: it proposes creating a fresh Python 3.12 venv and torch cu130 wheels, ignoring the existing working 3.11 venv (torch 2.11+cu128, CUDA verified on the RTX 5080 on this box); scope includes a Kotlin Android app, Jetson/Hailo runner, OSRM build, PMTiles build, 3-corporation tenancy and a 7-day plan where the differentiating depth code only arrives at Phase 2 step 7 and the credibility demo depends on 10-20 self-shot Hyderabad clips with tape measurements that nobody has collected. DBSCAN min_samples=1 at eps 6 m will happily merge adjacent potholes on bad GPS days. Licence awareness and IRC citations are good; the ₹7,396 vs ₹1,600 comparison is a strong jury hook.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: IMU-jolt observation record sent even without a camera detection (catches water-filled/night holes); 1 Hz trip_fix telemetry with cam_active flag so clean passes are provable; online camera-height drift monitoring via rolling median of RANSAC height per trip; thermal callbacks dropping fps on Snapdragon; depot Wi-Fi drain at 29 Greater Hyderabad depots; signed OTA model config; lateral-offset lane splitting of DBSCAN clusters; square-cut vs integrated cavity volume both stored to show savings.

scores.critique: The only design that treats depth measurement as a metrology problem rather than a model call: every measurement carries value + sigma + method tag (mono/mono_imu/stereo/lidar_phone/manual_gauge/citizen), with per-pixel sigma_Z = k*Z^2 propagated through the grazing angle (sigma_delta = sqrt(sigma_Z^2 sin^2 theta + plane_rms^2)), a local quadratic road surface for crown/rutting instead of a global plane, inverse-variance fusion with 3-sigma outlier rejection, and a per-device calibration certificate that gates Measurement Book billing. The staged foam-board target (20/40/70 mm) filmed with a checkerboard-calibrated phone at 5-12 m is the right credibility artefact for a jury and is doable on this dev box in an afternoon; it also keeps the DA3 scale-convention question configurable instead of asserted. It is the only design that actually inspected the environment correctly (existing Python 3.11 venv, torch 2.11+cu128, RTX 5080) and front-loads the measurement core (step 4) and a single-image end-to-end demo (step 6) so a partial build still demos. Weaknesses an ML reviewer should flag: the quarter-car IMU-to-depth model with a per-vehicle gain and '~15 % error' is over-claimed (jolt depends on speed, tyre, load, suspension state, and buses steer around holes); use it only as existence corroboration. DBSCAN min_samples=2 makes the 'candidate (1 pass)' state unreachable unless handled specially. The '12 depth frames/s at 518 px' throughput claim for DA3METRIC-LARGE on a 16 GB 5080 is optimistic. sigma_A = 2A*sigma_Z/Z ignores mask boundary error, which dominates area error for small holes. Scope is still enormous (Android, Jetson, OSRM, planetiler, PWA) and the 15-step build order is not time-boxed, but the ordering means risk is retired first. India fit is strong (GHMC charter, CRMP DLP, eMARG MB export, te/en SOP, 150/300 ward swap) though slightly thinner on day-to-day engineer workflow than Design 3.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: Measurement record with method + sigma + quality_score and billing gated on certified devices; local quadratic surface fit on the 0.3-1.0 m ring; sin(theta)-aware uncertainty propagation and fitted k from a truth set; staged known-depth foam-board target as the day-1 validation; pothole ground point = GPS + IPM range/bearing (not camera position); water-filled handling that never reports a water surface as floor; calibration certificate JSON with drift history; benchmarking all three depth backends on the same truth set.

scores.critique: Best 'government engineer will use it daily' design: full state machine with audit_log on every transition, escalation chain AE->DEE->EE->Zonal Commissioner, daily per-circle 'repair run' indent (bags, CRM, emulsion, crew-hours), jurisdiction queue for unknown road owners (directly addresses the Cyberabad CCTV pilot failure), HMDA and SCB included, Telugu field SOP, contractor scorecards, eMARG-pattern MB and invoice gating on verified_closed. The measurement science is adequate but weaker than Design 2 and contains one real engineering error: design depth is computed from d_avg (mean depth over the cut) rather than p95/max, so cold-mix will be under-ordered for the bowl-shaped holes that IRC says must be cut to sound material; the worked example (0.5x0.4 m, 'mean depth 60 mm' -> 3 bags) silently changes the convention the other designs use. Other issues: the error model sigma_D = 8 mm*(D/5)^2 is asserted, not fitted, and there is no sin(theta) term; 'depth_max = max (robust: 99th percentile)' is internally inconsistent; weighted-median/MAD fusion is fine but the CI is not a calibrated interval; the demo validation is on RDD2022 images with an assumed 1.4 m car calibration, which proves nothing about absolute depth (the synthetic rendered bowl test only checks integration maths, not model behaviour); pseudo-masking RDD boxes with a seg model trained on 3k eYantra images will yield worse masks than SAM2 box prompts. Feasibility: the hour-based 20-hour build order is not realistic for this scope; it plans torch 2.12 cu130 and a Python 3.14 API plus a separate 3.12 ML venv, ignoring the already-working 3.11+cu128 venv on the box. Credit for the pragmatic PostGIS nearest-way map-matching fallback that avoids an OSRM build for the demo, and for making DLP events evidence packages rather than automatic penalties (politically survivable). DBSCAN min_samples=2 has the same unreachable-candidate inconsistency as Design 2.
scores.best_ideas_to_steal: Daily per-circle repair run / indent with route ordering; jurisdiction queue for unresolved road ownership; audit_log with before/after JSON and field geolocation on every transition; escalation timers by AE/DEE/EE hierarchy; PostGIS nearest-way + heading map-match fallback for the demo; DLP events as evidence packages (before/after/re-detection) not auto-penalties; requiring 3 clean passes AND a 10 % random engineer QC sample before auto-close; Segmenter interface so YOLO26 (AGPL) can be swapped for RF-DETR (Apache) for government procurement; pluggable admin_unit table ready for the 300-ward re-delimitation.
